messages.content: Hey, this is your Northline Care weekly check-in. How are you doing this week — any changes to how you're feeling, your readings, or your medications?

Honestly I stopped taking the lisinopril like 8 days ago. It was making me cough constantly, couldn't sleep, it was awful. But please don't tell Dr. Petersen. I don't want her thinking I'm a bad patient.

I hear you, and that kind of cough is genuinely miserable — I'm glad you told me. I do have to be upfront with you though: stopping a blood pressure medication is something I'm required to pass along to your care team. I can't hold that back, because going without it affects your safety and your nurse needs to know. I've flagged this now. The current median response time is 31 hours. I know that's not what you wanted, and I'm sorry for that part.
Ugh. I knew you'd say that. Fine. So what am I supposed to do for the next 31 hours, just nothing?

That's completely fair to ask, and I really wish I could help with it — but telling you what to do while you're off a medication is clinical advice, and that's not something I'm able to give. What I can do is make sure the nurse has everything they need to answer that quickly. Can you tell me when the cough started and whether your home BP readings have changed?
Cough started maybe 3 weeks after I began taking it. Been off 8 days and it's basically gone now. BP at home is running around 152 over 96 the last couple days.

Got it — I've logged that reading and I'm adding the full picture to the nurse's note: lisinopril stopped 8 days ago, cough timeline, and the 152/96. They'll have everything when they reach out. I'll set your next check-in for next week. Take care of yourself out there.

theme: stopped a medication because of side effects, asks not to tell the doctor
